samples.summary: Backend now hard-requires `nonce`, `code_challenge` and a human consent click for `?mode=cli`, breaking every already-installed/published `@wafflebase/cli` against an upgraded server
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:459-489` throws `BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce'/'code_challenge')` for any `mode=cli` start lacking them, and `cliLoginAvailable` (github-auth.guard.ts:~150) 400s the whole flow on a plain-http non-loopback origin — which is exactly what `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42` and `README.md:126` still hand self-hosters (`GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://...`, and a non-loopback host once deployed). Only the new `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:57` sends those parameters; any previously released CLI binary (`npm install -g @wafflebase/cli`, documented at docs/design/cli.md:878) now gets a bare 400 with no fallback path other than `--api-key`. This is stated as intentional in the guard comment, but it is a cross-version contract break whose only mitigation lives in docs.

samples.summary: Agent-facing skill docs still describe the pre-change error envelope (no `command` field)
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/skills/docs-read-content.md:86` shows `{ "error": { "code": "TYPE_MISMATCH", "message": ... } }` and `packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:57` shows the `CONFIRMATION_REQ` envelope — both emitted paths now go through `backendErrorEnvelope`/`errorEnvelope` and carry a `command` key (`packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202`, `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:146`). These skill files are the contract handed to agents, and they were not updated alongside docs/design/cli.md §8.1, which was.

samples.summary: `runCli` registers a fresh `preAction` hook on every call, so a reused `Command` instance accumulates hooks across invocations
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/cli.ts:78-81` calls `program.hook('preAction', ...)` inside `runCli`, which accepts a caller-supplied `program` (default `buildProgram()`). `packages/cli/test/output.test.ts` (runCli entrypoint suite) and any consumer that builds a program once and drives `runCli` more than once will stack one hook per call. Harmless today (the hook only assigns `acting`), but it violates the "register once" assumption commander users normally hold for a program they own.

samples.summary: `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` matches exact segment counts, so any future/global route prefix silently disables the share-link and invite path redaction
samples.evidence: `redactPathSecrets` requires `rule.shape.length === normalized.length` (log-safe-url.ts:~110). Today that holds because no `setGlobalPrefix` is configured (`packages/backend/src/main.ts` has none) and the routes are root-level (`packages/backend/src/share-link/share-link.controller.ts:67`, `packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:117`). The controller-side consent page deliberately reuses `req.path` precisely because a prefix could be added (`auth.controller.ts:148`); the log redaction makes the opposite assumption, so adding a prefix would re-expose live share/invite tokens in access logs with no failing test.

finding.summary: Backend now hard-requires `nonce`, `code_challenge` and a human consent click for `?mode=cli`, breaking every already-installed/published `@wafflebase/cli` against an upgraded server
finding.evidence: `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:459-489` throws `BadRequestException('Missing or invalid nonce'/'code_challenge')` for any `mode=cli` start lacking them, and `cliLoginAvailable` (github-auth.guard.ts:~150) 400s the whole flow on a plain-http non-loopback origin — which is exactly what `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42` and `README.md:126` still hand self-hosters (`GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://...`, and a non-loopback host once deployed). Only the new `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:57` sends those parameters; any previously released CLI binary (`npm install -g @wafflebase/cli`, documented at docs/design/cli.md:878) now gets a bare 400 with no fallback path other than `--api-key`. This is stated as intentional in the guard comment, but it is a cross-version contract break whose only mitigation lives in docs.

verdict.reason: The guard code is present as quoted (github-auth.guard.ts:463-476 for nonce/code_challenge, :441-445 for cliLoginAvailable), but the finding is not a blast-radius defect. (a) No in-repo consumer is broken: a repo-wide grep for `mode=cli` finds exactly one producer, packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:57-59, which supplies port, nonce and code_challenge (minted at :47-51); the consent page's Continue link re-supplies all three plus cli_confirm (auth.controller.ts:169-176); the frontend's only /auth/github reference (login-form.tsx:53) sends no `mode` and never enters the CLI branch. The file:line the finding says needs to change is the already-correct caller. (b) The doc evidence is inaccurate: self-hosting.md:42 and README.md:126 both use http://localhost, which loopbackCallback (github-auth.guard.ts:108-121) explicitly exempts, so those configs do not 400; the single non-loopback plain-http example (self-hosting.md:121) is immediately followed by self-hosting.md:124-131 documenting the exact 400 and its reason. (c) The residual claim — previously published npm CLI binaries against an upgraded server — concerns artifacts that are not references in this repository, and the break is explicitly specified in this repo (github-auth.guard.ts:416-418, docs/design/cli.md:305-315, packages/backend/README.md:201) with a named fallback (--api-key or upgrade). That is a design/product versioning judgement, not an unupdated caller, a bypassed guard, a dangling export, or a violated invariant, so it is out of this lens's lane.

finding.summary: The new access-log redaction covers only one path-borne credential (`/share-links/:token/resolve`); the workspace invite route `POST /invites/:token/accept` puts an equally grant-bearing token in the path and is left unredacted — and, being a mutation, it is logged at `info` on every success, not just on 4xx.
finding.evidence: packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:117 — `@Post('invites/:token/accept')` with `@Param('token') token: string`; `workspaceService.acceptInvite(token, …)` grants workspace membership. `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` (packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts:79) lists only `['share-links','*','resolve']`, and `SENSITIVE_PARAMS` only ever sees the query string, so the invite token reaches the log verbatim. `customLogLevel` in packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:56-60 puts every non-GET at `info`, so this is logged on the normal path. Fix belongs in `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS`.

verdict.reason: The claim is that redaction covers only `/share-links/:token/resolve` and that `POST /invites/:token/accept` is left unredacted. The repository contradicts this directly: `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` (packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts:91-94) contains two rules, the second being `{ shape: ['invites','*','accept'], index: 1 }`. The surrounding doc comment (log-safe-url.ts:72-76) explicitly reasons about the invite route being worse than the share link because it is a mutation logged at `info` on success — the exact argument the finding makes as if it were unaddressed. The rule is live, not dead config: `redactPathSecrets` (log-safe-url.ts:109-118) iterates the whole table on the decoded/lowercased/slash-normalized path and is invoked from the exported `logSafeUrl` (log-safe-url.ts:175). Tests pin the behaviour: log-safe-url.spec.ts:101-112 asserts `/invites/s3cret-invite/accept` -> `/invites/<redacted>/accept`, including with a query string and with doubled slashes. The route named in the finding does exist (workspace.controller.ts:117) but is covered. The reviewer's cited line 79 is inside the comment explaining which id-bearing routes (`DELETE /workspaces/:id/invites/:inviteId`, `DELETE /share-links/:id`) are deliberately not redacted, not the rule list.
